Battlefield 6 is not a Battlefield game for Battlefield veterans. That, at its core, is fine. If Battlefield Studios want to cater to a different market, there is no problem with that. That said, as a long time franchise veteran, with thousands of hours across Bad Company 2, BF3, BF4, BF1, and BFV... I'm just tired, man. There are other reviews with walls of gripe about this game and those of them that mention previous experience with the franchise will all say the same thing: "this game isn't for us any more." The most glaring evidence of this is the removal of class-locked weapons, and even class-locked playlists. Gone, in pursuit of something very, very different. The maps are too crowded, too small, or too directionless. Remade maps have been shrunk, or changed to fit one particular playstyle; run and gun. A particular gripe of mine is how redundant snipers feel now. Never mind that every single sniper that has been added to the game is worse than the starting one, never mind that there is an attachment that literally zeroes the scope for you, removing half of the fun of figuring out hold points, never mind that an M4 with a couple of attachments will burst you down over 500+m quicker than you can rechamber a round if you miss your headshot... nobody even bothers. I see no snipers in this game, and when I do, they're running a rangefinder. It's boring. The remakes of Golmud and Firestorm? Boring. The small town at the top of Golmud, which was once a main thoroughfare that could be reliably held by a few well-placed engineers? Now a sprawling close-quarters arena, with too many angles to make defence a reliable option. Just let it get taken and attack again. All of the verticality, rocks that snipers could sit on? Flattened. There's one now, at the back of the map, obstructed by the same town with no view onto other objectives. Firestorm has been shrunk, and the petroleum containers on the right side of the map which once provided a little verticality are now destructible - all but guaranteeing that if you kill someone from there, they'll just get in a tank and blow it up so you can't use it. This game makes me physically tired to play. I'm not young. I don't particularly want to engage with the fast-paced, "sprint around like a headless chicken" form of play that this game all but incentivises. I never did in previous games, why would I want to now? Why are you giving me no other viable option? Look, if you like fast-paced close-quarters gameplay, then I'm sure this game is perfect for you, and I would encourage you to play it, to enjoy it. But for me, and so many others, who never sought that experience in Battlefield and knew that our playstyle was just as viable in all other entries to the franchise, even 2042 for goodness sakes... it's just not there, and it's clear that Battlefield Studios only intend to move further and further away from what this franchise used to be. What a disappointment. What a tremendous, saddening disappointment. --- Just to add a little amendment to the bottom here, as a lot of people have brought it up. I have played every battlefield game, that includes 1942 and even 2142, I just didn't play for hours upon hours with those games, at least not to the same extent that I did with the games I actually mentioned above. There's a lot of ♥♥♥ measuring going on in the comments about whether I'm a "true battlefield veteran," it's not that deep guys. I've been here from day 1, and love the older games, I just didn't grow up on them like I did the others so didn't mention them.

i hate to do this as much as the next guy but i genuinely felt like this game was actively trying to get me to stop playing from almost start to finish, spoilers ahead! before i begin let me clear up some things: this isn't a "waaah game's too difficult / everything does double damage / savage beastfly" review, i overall found the game's difficult to be mild at best and for a majority of the time easier or comparable to base hollow knight, just about everything dealing 2 masks of damage is a necessity as the game would just be pathetically easy otherwise, without the high damage you could quite literally tank and outheal bosses entirely, something i was STILL capable to in most mid to late game; i also don't think that everything about this game sucks or that silksong is the worst game ever, far from it, the art and music are fantastic, quite literally what you'd expect if you were to think of an enhanced hollow knight, perhaps i may be mis-remembering but it overall felt like the npcs in silksong were much more "alive" with many more player interactions which i appreciated; as for the story i can't really say much other than it's ok... but certainly didn't make me salivate to get into the lore and by the end of it i was so exhausted from everything the game pulled that i really just couldn't bother anymore; have you noticed how i haven't talked about the actual GAME yet? yeah let's talk about it. Hornet's base moveset feels amazing to play with, both fast and versatile, even equipped with a fancy new diagonal pogo move! surely the game is built around it yeah? nope, absolutely not even close and the hitbox of it is absurdly miniscule that using it in combat felt like a hindrance than an actual combat choice, in general the moveset just felt like it didn't belong in the game it was in and i couldn't help but feel that team cherry felt the same, what do i mean by that? well notice how i said "base" moveset, Hornet will gain access to different "crests" that change her moveset completely apart from meta-movement abilities, most of them are trash compared to the starter crest (keep this in mind), but one crest in particular... just gives you the hollow knight moveset and pogo, with a built in quick slash... the BEST tools (charms) distribution out of any crest AND a 2% chance to deal triple damage for no reason, wtf? i feel sorry to the 90+% of players that used this and robbed themselves out of experiencing silksong, you just played hollow knight 2. well ok surely that's not a complete deal breaker right? unfortunately it kinda is? remember how i mentioned almost every other crest just feels useless, because this is a big trend in this game, you'll feel weak no matter what, what do i mean by this? lightning round: -an impressive amount of tools are completely useless, there's no variety to builds as once you have the best stuff that's what you'll use and what everyone else will tell you to use. -upgrading your needle literally might as well not be a feature since enemies get a secret damage reduction, because why should you ever feel powerful traversing through early areas in a METROIDVANIA. -defensive upgrades like extra masks or max silk (soul) are so unbelievably far and few between that by the time you get your 7th mask, which is a huge deal when everything does 2 damage you're probably already done with 60% of the game, the 7th mask would be your SECOND HEALTH UPGRADE. -the only thing that "MAY" make you feel powerful, and this is a BIG may, are red tools, think of them kind of as one time throwing items, again most of them are dogs*** while 3-4 are actually worth using, problem is they require shards to craft, one of the 2 currencies in the game which... i really don't want to get into it but do know that despite making currencies more plentiful and stuff overall costing less in a patch i was STILL grinding for them deep into late-game, (this is accounting never losing ANY on dying twice before retrieving them); anyways, shards have a max capacity and if you're trigger happy with your red tools you've got 4-5 attempts at any given boss before you run out and have to grind because of course you don't get anything refunded if you die, great, safe to say i only ever used red tools when encountering particularly annoying bosses. (tl:dr) there is still a lot of stuff that i'd like to discuss in detail but it'd be a never-ending loop of things and minor design choices that ticked me off while i was playing so instead, i just want you to know this: this game hates you, the player, you WILL be inconvenienced at every step of the way, you WILL be ridiculed and made a fool of in practically every stage of the game, and just when you're about to say "surely it can't get worse than this" for the 4th time, it'll find a way to one up itself once more; Pharloom is an exceptionally dark and depressing place in the hollow knight universe, and so too will be your experience with it.

Beautiful presentation, hollow endgame, this one nails the classic gacha-MMO trap of looking incredible on the surface while the actual loop underneath wears thin fast. Pros ✔ Visuals are genuinely excellent, the anime art style is polished and the character creator gives real room to make something unique. ✔ Fashion and cosmetics are a major draw, with a wide variety of outfits and collab content like Monogatari and Fairy Tail. ✔ Strong initial presentation makes the first stretch of the game genuinely enjoyable for casual players. ✔ Good as a seasonal, low commitment anime MMO if you're not expecting long term depth. Cons ✘ The dye system is surprisingly restrictive, several collab outfits don't allow full recoloring, undercutting the customization the game is otherwise praised for. ✘ Story is largely forgettable, more about moving between zones than giving you a reason to care. ✘ Endgame loop is shallow and repetitive, the same daily gather, craft, and boss run routine with minimal variation. ✘ Progression heavily gatekept by Ability Score requirements in group content, making it hard to advance without already being carried. ✘ Dungeon design recycles the same handful of layouts across difficulty tiers rather than offering real variety. ✘ Seasonal resets wipe progress and restart the grind, turning what should feel rewarding into a treadmill. ✘ Best cosmetics are locked behind limited-time gacha banners, adding a monetization layer on top of an already repetitive structure. Overall Blue Protocol: Star Resonance has a genuinely strong foundation, gorgeous presentation, solid character customization, and an inviting first impression. But the endgame doesn't hold up, seasonal resets undercut long-term investment, and progression leans too heavily on gatekeeping and gacha luck. Worth trying for a season if you want something casual and pretty, not worth committing to as a long-term MMO. Rating 4/10

Everyone uses the word "masterpiece" loosely; however, this game reminds you every second that it is made by masters of their craft. It embodies in every way the correct philosophy that should lead the future of game design. Craftsmanship is found in every facet of the game, be it invisible aspects like the optimization of graphical performance, or more striking elements like the research and artisanship that led to such a beautiful world, full of history, and so faithful that every building, every tree, every creek, every person, absolutely everything, looks exactly as you would expect if you went back in time. Even the little details are full of passion and history, like the loading icon or the breathtaking paintings in the loading screen; they look as if painted in another century. The feeling you get while playing the game is that you truly are in a living, breathing world. Absolutely nothing is bland; everything emanates love and craftsmanship. Additionally, if you take into account all the possible interactions and complex systems used in this game and how well they work, every other game feels so bare bones, bland, and backwards. This game is so full of things to love, that it is impossible to express in a few words how amazing it really is.

After returning to Arena breakout from its Beta/season 1-3 and joined back mid season 6, I have to say this game has actually gotten better overall. Now to be said there are still flaws, however 90% of the criticism it is receiving is not actually part of the game or genuine issues. Recently they added zombies, this is getting a bit of backlash due to "It no longer being a realistic shooter and now its just another arcade shooter." First off, if you played beta, or even kept up with story line, this has been teased, and part of the story for a while, so "zombies" were to be expected. With that said, they are not that bad, they look good, move good and sound good. HOWEVER, they are redundant, there is not anything special about them. Overall its just a wash. I like them, they are not that bad, however I see the complaints. Another one is the removal of hostile Sector. This is honestly the only bad change this update. There are MANY players that play for pure PVE alone(I am not one of them so idc, but I will miss it) Hostile sector was a challenge for most, and actually required skill and time. It also filled that missing spot for PVE players. Yes there is still PVE but its only the endless zombies, or No mans land. No mans land would be fine, if it were challenging or intense. However you can just waltz through like its nothing, and you cannot go into it for free if you run out of passes. Cheaters, still a problem, like any game, however in 90% of other games, they do not get noticed because you are not truly effected by them, you just die and respawn or lose and invo of loot(Like rust or DayZ). This however you lose a lot, and its much harder to fight cheaters. However in my 120+ hours since I started playing again, I've ran into 2 cheaters. This is all in lockdown or forbidden zone as well. They are a problem, and always will be, just as any game. We can only hope their Anti cheat or catching process gets better to catch them more and faster. (also to help prevent) The people complaining about PVP. Idk wtf they are on about. PVP this season was saved. No more armor piercing RNG, no more pointless headshots or bullets just ricocheting off the helmet. Yes time to kill went up, but its a better thing, it allows the worse players a chance to outplay, or gives the better players rewarding good aim (headshots etc). ITs also such a small amount, but its so much better not getting one shot by a T4/T5 bullet while wearing full T5/T6. For anyone that wants to check this game out but gets worried about the reviews, take them, including this one, with a grain of salt. Try it out, only you can decide if you like it. Personally, I do love this game, it runs great, feels great. Its a blast, and I enjoy playing it even when I get ♥♥♥ on. right now its a solid 8.5/10. I would highly recommend checking it out. **I played about 50+/hrs on their original launcher before steam release**

A PVP focused Extraction Shooter where the PVP aspect is by far the weakest part. First the positives: -easy to pick up -easy gun customization -easy Call of Duty-esque get back into action quick playstyle -nice graphics -nice sound design: overall sound design not talking about footsteps in particular -good variety of maps and loot the in-between: -player driven economy -relatively decent exploration even outside of the main POIs -ability to play what you like -"tiered" progression -satisfying loot experience (more prior to recent update now not so much anymore further detail in the lower section) the bad: -directional audio: it's buggy sometimes, esp when it comes to elevation changes -gunfights: this gets picked up in the next section further down so look there for an explanation -current looting experience: since the latest update you now immediately know if an item is high in value or not bc high value items now take longer to be identified compared to regular items the ugly: -cheating: yes they ban cheaters, yes they have an anti-cheat, does it stop ppl from cheating? well ofc iit does not, every MP game will have that problem and i am fully aware of that, the problem here is that your loadout is on the line so if you have a high value loadout you're much more likely to store it then to use it or you play iin secure-ops where you can't lose your loot -economy: some players have millions upon millions if not billions extracted, you get to keep you money past "wipes" so those players have an immediate advantage over new players and can diictate market prices, yes the game does combat that somewhat by giving out tier 4 gear like candy but that doesn't help against artificial inflation of ammo and gear prices esp above tier 4 -gunfights: Part 1 PVE: like i said above, the point returns, why? Bc it fits both categories, gunfights against bots are by enlarge mundane and more nuisance than challenge, i get it just like in Arc Raiders the bots are supposed to be a nuisance that you have to take into calculation for gunfights and can use as an asset, the only exception to this are bosses and the additional spawns alongside them as they usually carry higher tier gear, react faster etc. i'm not saying bots should be as overpowered as they are/were in Gray Zone Warfare but i wish there would be different tiers of AI and esp the AI in TV-Station, inside Armory and inside the Hotel on Northridge could def pose more of a threat than they do now. Part 2 PVP: gunfights in PVP are insanely hit or miss, either you get matched with people with full Tier 6 armor, H416 or Mosin with Tier 7 ammo, usually in a duo, trio or squad stack or you get matched against people doing corpse runs i.e. standard kit, no helmet <200k loot value, no in between, the former you will not win against nor will they lose any money while "risking" their gear bc their friends will just pick up what they had on and exfil right away, the latter you prob spend more money than you gain, this is by no means exclusive to ABI but it somehow feels unfair nonetheless -matchmaking: if you're a new player who just started out and you get matched against seasonalnolife557 with 20bn extracted tell me where the balancing is, one risks his loadout with the potential of going broke while the other sits on stacks of cash throwing one Mosin with full red ammo and 50 slot backpack filled with nades and stims into the raid one after another without a care in the world part of the experience? absolutely, the norm? it shouldn't be. -PVP: by far the worst part of the game, the game has to my knowledge 24-tickrate servers, that is quite abysmal, heavy desyncs are a feature, trust me, i do not know why they even feature a killcam when 90% of the kills look like they're cheated but are simply a problem of desync, overall the PVP aspect is heavily unbalanced and in many cases actually unfun, why can people bring full tier 5 gear and an M4 with a semi decent kit 60 round mags full of tier 4 ammo into a raid with a value cap of 450k, well simple, they cheat the system, bc mags can be stored in backpacks and do not contribute to equipment value that way, worn armor is valued less than new armor, which makes sense but then you should add a gear cap instead restrict the items ppl can bring into a raid by making it so the lowest mode (450k equip value) can only be tier 3 or lower and do not allow crafted items, then for the next difficulty make it tier 4 + 5 only (unable to queue with tier 6 stuff but able to queue with <tier 4) and then lastly a open difficulty where absolutely everything goes but a minimal amount of loot value has to be equipped (basically like it is now) -high value loot (red items): prob the most dividing point of criticism i have but i think high value loot (red items) should not be allowed in safe storage, yes they are rare and insanely valuable but exactly due to that reason it should be high risk, high reward, not, get lucky, store in safe container and don't care anymore, PVP is the center of the game, therefore it would only make sense if red items could not be stored in a safe box and instead drives up the risk and adds more tension in an otherwise, "oh red, nice *put in safe*, *runs to exfil*, *dies*, eeeh whatever at least i got 1.6 mill loot value :)" scenario.

Kingdom Come Deliverance 2 is my favourite game of 2025. I started playing the first game this time last month, and finished with the second game just now. Henry's journey from a peasant boy to one of gaming's most compelling heros mirrors the studio Warhorse's journey from scrapping together whatever money they could find to develop a realistic, medieval RPG to fill the hole that The Elder Scrolls has left in our hearts. Only, they did this with realistic gameplay, and zero magic systems. Their ability to make the mundane lives of peasantry and the politicking of nobles and lords be so interesting is a strong indicator of how well the writing team at Warhorse is. Daniel Vavra's experience as an industry veteran, plus unshakeable belief in their game has given us two of the best RPGs in gaming. While KCD1 was a proof of concept, KCD2 is a celebration that their concept works, and how well it can translate to being one of the best games of all time, if not the most important game of 2025. After playing the hell out of MH world (500hrs ~ ,had to stop myself from playing coz it was so good and addicting) I decided to give MH wilds a go, bought it at a 58% off discount. This game irked me and felt wrong from the very beginning. The boring story. At first I thought it was translation but it felt just as bad no matter if I played it in English/Spanish/polish/Japanese. Characters. Erik and his distracting lip filler looking duck lips. The whiny 12, year old Nata. Massive non memorable map layouts that u just pass though on your Uber mount.(Takes you automatically everywhere). You can walk but it's not efficient since theyr scaled the map with the mounts in mind. 90% of the game felt brain-dead easy. Fights on average are shorter, and with the wound system monsters often lay down more than they stand. You can go through most of the game without paying attention to the elements/charms/debuffs/. Just craft weapon with best stats, armour with best stats, and no need to think. Then suddenly at the end it's like they wake up to the fact that there's no much challenge and add a few harder monsters. The difficulty jumps feels jarring too, it's like the game fails to prepare you. Monsters look nice, however fights against them left less of a memorable impression on me than those in world. Character creation is much better too. Weapons/Armours looked great. Graphically it's overall much better than world/rise. The ability to carry 2 weapons is another thing that I liked. But overall this game felt like whatever hardship/annoyance there was, has been removed, smooth experience without friction. It certainly was made with casuals in mind. The difficulty was equivalent of playing MH world with defender gear on. No tracking, monster is visible right away, gathering is much easier too. Right away they allow the usage of AI hunters to aid you. This game is one step away from playing itself. We all know that base game is half of the experience, my opinion of the game might be more positive once the dlc drops. For now, I'm not too impressed.

I think by now everyone has played or at least heard about Clair Obscure: Expedition 33, but I'm not going to spoil anything about the game in this review. The story is about a group of people living in an isolated town called Lumiere, inspired by France during the Belle Époque. A huge number can be seen on the monolith that the Paintress paints every year, which affects them, so they form a team of expeditioners to sail to her in hopes of killing her and stopping her from harming the people in Lumiere. This year, Expedition 33 is gathering to start the adventure. Will they be able to stop her and live life normally? The gameplay is like that of old RPGs, where you explore a world map, travel from city to city, meet people, kill monsters, and upgrade your weapons. The fighting is turn-based, which I'm familiar with. Think of old Final Fantasy games when you play this game. It is clear it was inspired by those old games, and the atmosphere is similar to NieR, which is one of my favorite games. However, there is no manual save; the game autosaves regularly. Whenever you find a flag checkpoint, it will save automatically and let you fast-travel to another checkpoint. Make sure to touch the checkpoint flag whenever you want to save. The combat is turn-based with QTEs, which you can set to auto in the settings if that's not your thing. Each character has a different fighting style and set of skills. The only things I had to do repeatedly were parrying attacks and dodging. I found out that by learning and hearing the attack, it would be easy to parry it. It frustrated me a couple of times, especially with some bosses you can't kill unless you parry them, but you can always fail and learn how to do it next time. The game needs some grinding to kill some bosses. Try not to skip any monsters you see around; kill them to level up and earn new weapons. The artwork is outstanding, and every detail in the game is beautiful and meaningful. The color palette chosen for each area is mesmerizing, and the character's design is memorable. This game did something other games in my opinion failed to do. There is no UI and clutter while you are exploring the areas; you just walk around and enjoy each detail without having a health bar, a minimap, or a distracting list of objectives. You have the full screen to yourself and your character, which is a huge plus for me, as it lets me enjoy the environment. The characters' animations and facial expressions are on point; you can see the emotions in their gazes, posture, and voices. The voice actors did an outstanding job capturing the essence of those characters. It felt like watching a movie; in each scene, you could see how they reacted, what they looked like, and how they received each piece of information. This alone makes you want to replay the game to watch those little details. The dialogues are extremely well written. Music is breathtakingly beautiful; each soundtrack is meaningful; the lyrics tell a story and capture the characters' emotions. The game has 154 tracks on the main album alone, worth listening to, and they will actually stick in your head after playing the game. Character development is one of the strong suits of this game; you can see and feel how they bond, how they become stronger, how they hate, and how they grow suspicious. The writing of each character is phenomenal, especially in Act 2. Pros: +Emotional beautiful story. +Outstanding soundtracks. +Beautiful graphics and animations. +Great characters and monsters design. +Phenomenal voice over. +Turn-based combat. +World map. +Fast traveling. +Journal. +Multiple endings. +Collectables. +Cosmatics for each character. +Auto save. +Steam achievements. Cons: - No manual save. The game is unique in that it doesn't explain the story to you directly; it wants you to follow it emotionally and logically, forming theories about what is going on before the grand reveal. I highly recommend not charging and just killing bosses without exploring the world, reading the journals, or speaking to the characters. Those interactions will give you different layers to the story, and you'll understand it more, especially in the last act, where you'll be able to explore the whole map to read more information and learn more about the characters. The game has two endings; it is up to you how you want this to end. For more reviews check my curator page Feena's Choice Follow IndieGems for more reviews like this one.

I had a conversation with a friend on Discord recently about Where Winds Meet and they asked my thoughts on it, so instead of a standard review I'm just going to post that reply here: Saebin — 22:26 I think "Online RPG" describes Where Winds Meet accurately. Kinda like the original Guild Wars. Online, but you actually can ignore that element almost entirely and choose not to interact with it. It's not unheard of, just kind of rare in more well-known games or games that have/had a budget behind them. Overall to me it's built like a mobile game in terms of it's sub-menus and sub-systems (Maybe even worse). The gameplay and story are solid up until endgame, delivering exactly on what the game sells itself as and shows in trailers. You can do just about anything in this game, even pretty much fly and ontop of that even build. However, the wild and over the top eastern mythology here at play and the story is what will keep most invested and wanting to continue playing in the end. There is a currency limitations in Where Winds Meet (WWM) and I believe the currency limitation actively holds back WWM since players cannot do things at their own pace - this is probably done to create a returning playerbase more than anything, but that strategy is likely to also see players leave like I did in the end. It's a fun game at least worth checking out since it's free, but, if you do reach endgame you'll find very little reason to stay when you ask yourself "What am I actually doing this for?" because the answer to that is "Just to see larger numbers in a mostly singleplayer experience." or "Just to unlock a hard to obtain skill that'll just increase my numbers slightly and change part of my rotation and style in combat for a bit." and those novelties wear off pretty quickly in a mostly singleplayer adventure when you're done with the storylines and the mystery of exploration and learning new mechanics. While I do recommend the game, I don't think it's worth keeping installed once you're "Done" due to the significant amount of real estate it demands from a hard drive (Nearly 200gb), especially when you are limited in currency gains which you don't truly feel until endgame. So to me... It's a one and done game. (Reply ends here.) Note to the Devs: Do a currency crunch, it was getting a little silly when I last played - probably worse now. What I mean is unify many of the existing currencies into a singular one and remove the limitations on gaining them. Good luck and all the best. It was a fun and wild experience which definitely delivered, especially for a free game.

Possibly the best game I've ever played and the best game humanity has ever seen. It has the best RPG mechanics of all time for sure. You can be whoever you want and the game allows it, because you can complete every quest through various routes depending on your character. There are so many ways to complete quests, it's really cool. It features a great story with well-written characters. I like how it is based on real history with real historical figures, and the epic of some story moments is impressive. I also love the side quests in this game, they can be a bit boring sometimes, but in general, I really like them. I've completed every side quest and activity I've seen on both maps, though. I also like the realism in this game, it's really cool how characters react to Henry depending on how clean he is or what clothes he's wearing. The devs also did a really great job making map exploration interesting. I've explored every point of interest on both maps and it was awesome. Some discoveries led to interesting situations or even mini-quests, and Henry's reactions to certain things even change depending on where you are in the story. The combat system makes this game even more interesting than it already is. Compared to KCD1, master strikes have become much cooler and more interesting to use. Plus, I like the variety of marksman weapons now. We used to only have bows in KCD1, but now we have crossbows and guns, which is really cool. I also like that there are three romance storylines, compared to KCD1 where there was only one. In general, the devs are geniuses, and the game is a masterpiece. I'd say they took everything that was already good in the first game and even improved it. Also, I'd like to thank the developers for adding the Ukrainian language to the game. There aren't many devs who do this, and it is really pleasant that I can play in my native language.

Steam's review system isn't nuanced enough, so I want to say that this is still generally a worthwile game, but you need to know what you're getting into. The ambiance is perfect. Beautifully rendered and grounded environments. Most of my time was staring into the horizon and little nooks in the scenery indoors. It's so well lit, that my phone took better screenshots than whatever HDR-to-SDR conversion happened in the computer. The fricking 3D paperdoll rotating inventory is so cool I would sometimes just switch tabs idly to see it go. The story is enjoyable, a good context and motivation for the player's action. But is in equal measures varied and incredibly railroaded. Some (main quest) missions have only 1 correct solution, and if your build is not tailored to that you are just ♥♥♥, go load a previous save and grind ♥♥♥ stealth or alchemy or whatever it is. The world is very detailed visually, but it's all very "look, don't touch". You think there would be for example a way to bypass stealth with craftsmanship in a certain place, but nope, you have to take the 1 exact route the designer chose. There's also some clear "sequel one-upsmanship" going on here, which usually play into the railroading. There could be a straightforward solution in the moment, but the game does not give you the tools to take it. I can't elaborate without getting into spoilers, but it really feels sometimes like watching a horror movie protagonist do something clearly stupid even in context. It's a movie with a lot of gameplay, to the point that it might actually have been better served by being a sandbox open world game with an accopmpanying movie, I feel like it would have been less frustratng that way.

TL;DR: Great game, worse Hollow Knight. 8/10 For context: the original Hollow Knight is my favorite game of all time. I've beaten it deathless and without upgrading my character. So when I say Silksong frustrated me, it's not a skill issue rant. If Hollow Knight gives you a wall and tells you to go find a pickaxe, Silksong expects you to break through it with your head. The good Movement is god-tier. Hornet glides through levels like a ballerina. Traversal is so fluid it's basically its own form of fun, so the huge map never feels like a chore to cross. Combat has depth. Pogo, parries, deflecting projectiles, tools (spears, knives, potions, grenades), and Crests that completely change your moveset or healing. You can build a mage, a tool spammer, whatever you want. Exploring new areas is the best part. Almost every biome brings new enemies, mechanics and upgrades. Greymoor, Shellwood, Deep Docks and the Citadel are phenomenal, classic Metroidvania design. Art and music are stunning. Tons of tiny details, multilayered backgrounds, and another incredible Christopher Larkin soundtrack. Story and lore are coherent and well thought out, and Hornet actually talking makes the narrative much easier to follow. The bad Less Metroidvania, more Souls. Many areas are fairly linear with shortcuts. You clear them on the first pass and never come back. Backtracking often leads to a room with a handful of rosaries. Some secrets are absurdly hidden , Dark Souls illusory wall style. Good luck getting 100% without a guide. The balance feels like a stream challenge run. HK's endgame damage (2 masks per hit) becomes the default a few hours in, while your HP stays at base level. Getting knocked into spikes by a boss can take 4 masks in a second. The new healing (3 masks at once, but only with full silk) is the only thing that makes this work. If you get chunked with no silk, you need 9 hits on 1 HP to heal. Stingy direct progression. Twice as many silk upgrades as HK for the same endpoint. Your first needle upgrade is basically it until Act 2. One extra mask barely matters when you die in 3 hits anyway. "Rage-game" design. A bench that's a trap (the only one in the whole game, using the same assets), a boss that explodes on death and nearly one-shots you, flying enemies that fall on you for double damage. Consequences way out of proportion to the mistake. Gauntlets everywhere. Locked-arena wave fights every 15 minutes against enemies you've already beaten, often copy-pasted arenas, often with no reward at all (drops disabled). One mandatory 10-wave gauntlet ends in a boss, so every death means 10 more minutes to try again. Lazy bosses. Few of them, many with 2 to 4 attacks spammed at high speed and high damage. Lots of them spawn random adds, so RNG decides how hard the fight is. Some are recycled up to three times as mandatory fights. Broken economy. Paid benches are fine (rosary strings exist for that), but shop prices are huge and about half the enemies drop nothing. You WILL farm rosaries, and shell shards too if you rely on tools. Little to no rewards. Many bosses give nothing, one 30-minute area gives you... a Steam achievement. Clearing a zone for an hour gets you 30 rosaries. For a game with speedrun and deathless achievements, this kills replay value. Quests are MMO-style fetch/kill tasks, a leftover from when Silksong was a DLC, and they're mandatory to reach the endgame. Courier quests are basically mini platforming Death Stranding: you'll either love them or hate them. Minor bugs : bosses vanishing between phases and just dying, broken scripts, inconsistent hitboxes. Rare, and the devs are patching quickly. Act 3 (spoilers) Story-wise it's great fanservice that ties up most threads from HK. Lace's arc feels chaotic and underexplained, and Grandmother Silk appears in like two scenes, so the antagonist never really lands. Gameplay-wise, the jump to the endgame is barely noticeable because the whole game already had endgame balance. Most side bosses give nothing or near-useless items. And the final boss of a multi-dozen-hour game is... a third Lace fight with extra AoE attacks, partly recycled from other enemies. Seriously? The whole act feels rushed and done on the cheap: barely any new areas, recycled enemies, and the difficulty bump is just the same modifiers slapped on everything. Verdict The core gameplay is impeccable, and most of the problems show up only when you dig into the details, so you might not even notice them. This is for HK veterans who want a bigger challenge and Souls fans who like platformers. If you're new to hard games, it might break you. Hollow Knight is a 9/10 for me. Silksong is an 8/10 , and at its price it's still one of the biggest, highest-quality games you can buy.

Instead, I found out the game is leaving Game Pass just three days after it's anniversary. Pulling it from Game Pass with no anniversary event, no acknowledgment, and no update feels like a huge misstep. It sends a message to the community that the game is being quietly dropped. Why would I pay to own this game if I'm made to believe there will be no future content or updates? Buy it on sale for a couple hours of enjoyment, but don't expect it to be worth full price. In fact, you'll prolly enjoy the game more if you're not familiar with souls games, cuz you won't be comparing it to the flawlessly accurate melee combat and deep, organic exploration that you get from fromsoft. The best thing about this game is the presentation. There are some memorable music tracks and the graphics are created very competently, even if I found most of the character and enemy designs to be uninteresting. The gameplay leaves much to be desired, with boring combat that does not evolve at all throughout the game and movement abilities that are restrictive and limit player expression. Bosses feel unpolished and rarely have more than 2-3 attacks. For example there is an early boss that has a total of 2 attacks both of which it takes long enough to recover from that you can heal fully every time, making the boss almost impossible to die to. The level designs are usually a straight path to the boss with a few dead end paths with items and optional encounters which would be fine in a level based game but feels counter-intuitive in a Metroidvania. The game also is buggy, for example pop in and unwanted text being added to descriptions. Play The Last Faith or Blasphemous first.

This is a classic Kairsoft game. There is a low-skill threshold, you do not play golf, you just design and grow the course with simple drag and drop controls. It is a macro not micro-management game, you donâ€TMt have to hire staff, set prices or sculpt topography. The gameplay loops overlap beautifully, new holes need to balance difficulty with scenery to attract new members, advertising campaigns & tournaments boost players and, in a timing mini game you coach your players so they can win tournaments. All contributing to the requirements to rank up your club to the next star to unlock more course and clubhouse design options. It is a slow and somewhat therapeutic gameplay experience that will have you looking at your watch wondering how did this much time pass. It does not revolutionize the genre, but it does distill the expertise of developer who has done this many times and it makes for a great gaming sorbet between M Rated FPS and 100 hr RPG

You like horror and I mean the twisted, sick, demented gruesome kind then you gotta try this. It's simple, what I've played so far anyway but it may be harder than you think unless you are good at the old pen & paper type hangman game and also unscrambling words. It gives a hint on hangman but it's not often helpful much IMO. Aftter a few successful words unscrambles, you start to catch on to the type of words it likes to use. The text dialogue from the killer sharing thoughts is cool. Take too long to guess an answer and get a fun surprise. Fail on a round and anotther fun surprise, to see how the family member you picked to die is snuffed out. End of the rounds when all are dead, get a cool horror cutscene with the killer & you which I've seen 2 different ones (so may be more) it has alternated between. The sound of the killer walking around in the room is a nice touch to the mood and I recommend listening through your stereo or headphones for better horror effect.
